subject: Enterprise SLO evidence & measurement — proposed approach and handoff
messages:
From: procurement@novushealth.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP: Service guarantees, measurement methodology, and evidence package

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking our RFP. As part of Novus Health's procurement process we need a clear description of how Redwood measures uptime and latency for enterprise customers, what evidence you will provide during onboarding and ongoing audits, and the service credit calculation. Specifically: 

- Precise definitions: what endpoints/metrics are used to compute uptime and which requests are considered (control plane only, control+data plane, or customer-facing API)?
- Latency: are percentiles computed on successful request completion only? How is batching and token length normalized?
- Sampling & probes: cadence of synthetic probes vs production sampling; any regional weighting applied?
- Attribution: how do you attribute incidents for private/dedicated deployments vs hosted customers?
- Evidence delivery: types of logs/traces you will share, retention windows, and format (CSV, JSON, signed summaries).
- Credit formula: we prefer a deterministic monthly credit formula and an explanation of maintenance windows and exclusion events.

Please respond with a short methodology document and note any limitations (e.g., telemetry access for on-prem installs). We plan to include your response in our technical evaluation and security review.

Regards,
Jai Singh
Novus Health — Procurement
[Attachment: Novus-RFP-Section-4.pdf (PDF)]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: procurement@novushealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: Service guarantees, measurement methodology, and evidence package

Hi Jai — thank you, and great questions. Attached is a concise methodology summary (Redwood-SLO-Measurement.pdf) and an appendix with probe specs. Highlights below; I can schedule a 90-minute measurement workshop if helpful.

1) Uptime definition
- Uptime (availability) is measured at the customer-facing API gateway (ingress). We report a monthly availability percentage computed as: 1 - (total seconds of unavailability during the month / total operational seconds in the month). Unavailability is defined as inability to establish a successful request/response for the nominal API surface (token generation / chat endpoints).
- Control-plane-only outages (e.g., config UI) are reported separately and do not count against data-plane availability unless they impact API traffic.

2) Latency measurement
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) are computed on successful 2xx responses for the configured API route.
- To normalize across workloads we provide: a) a canonical 1k-token synthetic payload for probe baselining, and b) request-size buckets for production sampling (<=32 tokens, 33-512, 513-1024, >1024). Percentiles are reported per bucket and aggregated with weighting by request-class volume.
- Batching: when server-side batching is enabled, we report both per-request latency and per-batch latency; the SLOs reference per-request latency unless otherwise negotiated.

3) Sampling & synthetic probes
- Production sampling: default 1% sampled request tracing (configurable).
- Synthetic probing: global probes at 5-minute cadence per region, and a configurable 1-minute fast-check for high-SLA customers. Probes exercise the same API surface and payloads as production baselines.
- Region weighting: metrics are aggregated using traffic-weighted averages across regions. If Novus prefers region-specific SLOs we can expose per-region windows.

4) Attribution & private/dedicated deployments
- Hosted: attribution uses Redwood telemetry and synthetic probes.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed): same as hosted; we can provide tenant-scoped logs and signed evidence.
- Private/on-prem: we provide an evidence-handoff specification. For air-gapped deployments, Redwood supplies a signed telemetry export tooling specification (checksumed tarball) and an audit checklist; availability assertions for on-prem are based on signed export + customer-side telemetry.

5) Evidence package
- On request we provide: raw telemetry CSV (timestamps, region, route, response-code, latency-ms, token-count), tracer spans for sampled requests, synthetic probe logs, and a signed monthly summary PDF. Retention: production telemetry retained for 90 days by default (extendable). Formats: CSV/JSON for raw, PDF for executive summaries.

6) Credit formula & exclusions
- Standard credit: Credits are calculated monthly as a percentage of the monthly Redwood bill for the affected service.
- Example: for 99.9% monthly availability target, credit = min(50% of monthly bill, ((target - measured)/target) * 100%). (We are open to negotiating a different cap.)
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (>=48h notice), customer-induced outages, third-party upstream outages with verified root cause, and force majeure events.

Attachments: Redwood-SLO-Measurement.pdf, probe-spec-appendix.xlsx (appendix includes CSV column spec).

Next steps: if this aligns with Novus' expectations I suggest a measurement workshop (60–90 mins) with our SRE and CS teams where we walk through telemetry examples and a sample evidence bundle.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: Redwood-SLO-Measurement.pdf (PDF); Attachment: probe-spec-appendix.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: jai.singh@novushealth.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: Service guarantees, measurement methodology, and evidence package

Aditya — thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A couple clarifying items before we move to a workshop: 

- For private / on-prem customers: will Redwood sign and timestamp the telemetry export and include a SHA256 checksum? We will need chain-of-custody evidence for our auditors.
- For latency p99: does the metric include ingress queuing/edge retries, or is it measured after request reaches the first Redwood worker?
- If we enable server-side batching for cost reasons, can you provide an expected token-level p99 (i.e., amortized across tiny vs large requests) or do you only provide per-request?

Also, please confirm retention guarantees if Novus opts into extended 2-year storage for audit purposes — any cost estimate would be helpful.

Regards,
Jai
Novus Health — Procurement

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: RFP: Service guarantees, measurement methodology, and evidence package

Aditya — quick internal notes before your workshop with Novus.

- Credit cap: recommend we propose default cap at 50% monthly bill, but offer 75% for enterprise negotiated SLAs. We should avoid open-ended liability.
- Queueing boundary: product teams prefer to exclude network ingress retries outside our edge (i.e., p99 measured at the Redwood ingress that has application-layer visibility). We need to be explicit in the workshop.
- Batching guidance: request we provide both per-request and token-normalized estimates in the sample CSV. Can you prepare a 2-row CSV snippet showing how aggregated percentiles map to request-count vs token-count?

Attaching a draft credit matrix for your reference. If this goes to legal we should mark maintenance notice requirements clearly (>=48h unless emergency).

Thanks — LM

[Attachment: credit-matrix-draft.csv (CSV)]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: procurement@novushealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: Service guarantees, measurement methodology, and evidence package

Hi Jai — quick follow-up with clarifications and a proposed workshop time.

Clarifications: 
- Chain-of-custody for on-prem exports: yes — Redwood will provide a signed, timestamped telemetry export and include a SHA256 checksum for the delivered artifact. We will also provide an audit checklist describing collection commands and the checksum verification steps.
- Latency boundaries: p99 includes the application-side ingress we operate (TLS termination + request parsing + queuing on Redwood workers). It excludes external network hops before our edge. We will document the exact packet/flow boundaries in the technical appendix.
- Batching: we will provide both per-request and token-normalized percentile tables. The appendix includes a small example mapping per-request p99 to token-level p99 using weighted aggregation and sample request distributions.
- Retention: standard telemetry retention is 90 days. Extended retention (1–2 years) is available as an add-on; I'll include a rough cost estimate in the workshop materials (typically ~0.8–1.5% of monthly hosted spend per year of extra retention depending on granularity).

Proposed workshop: Tue, Nov 18, 2025 — 10:00–11:30 PT. We'll include SRE (telemetry), Product (measurement), and CS (onboarding). Please confirm attendees and any additional questions to include in the agenda.

I've uploaded the detailed appendix and a signed introductory summary to the shared folder: https://redwood-drive.example.com/novus/slo-evidence and sent the patterned SOW via DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/8A7F23

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Best regards,
Aditya Rao
